To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the FadL protein is required for the uptake of long chain fatty acids in E. coli, that the uptake is regulated by the osmotic environment of the cell, that the FadR protein is the positive regulator of fadL transcription, and that the OmpR protein, in the presence of the EnvZ protein, acts as a repressor of fadL gene expression.
osmolarity regulates transcription of the fadle gene in E. coli by the OmpR EnvZ two-component system, and that the FadR represses transcription of the fadla gene.
osmotic upshock causes the phosphorylation of OmpR by EnvZ, which in turn binds to the fadL regulatory region and represses transcription of the fadle gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the uptake of long chain fatty acids by E.coli.
the osmotic regulation of the fadl gene in Escherichiacoli.
the osmotic regulation of the FadR and OmpR-EnvZ systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FadL protein is a component of the outer membrane that functions in the transport of fatty acids.
the OmpR/EnvZ two-component regulatory system regulates transcription of the faddL gene in E. coli by direct interaction with the promoter region.
the fadL operon is regulated by the Osmoregulatory Two-Component Signal Transduction System (OmpR/EnvZ) and that the FadR protein is a repressor of the fad operon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FadL is a protein that is involved with the uptake of long chain fatty acids, and is osmotically controlled.
osmolarity affects the transcription of the FadR protein, and the OmpREnVZ two-component system regulates the transcription of the fadaL gene in response to the environmental osmolarity.
osmotic stress represses fadL transcription by the action of the OmpRENVZ two-component system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FadR protein is a repressor of the fadR gene and is not involved in osmotic regulation of the gene.
the OmpREvZ two-component system is involved in the osmoregulation of the fadl gene, but it does not explain how the FadL protein itself contributes to osmoregulation.
the OmpREnvsystem is involved in the regulation of fatty acid uptake.
